quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: At the swimming pool, children under ten must wear a bright orange armband. The lifeguard checks every child before they enter the water.
quests.question: A nine-year-old must wear an armband at the pool.
quests.hint: Think about which ages count as "under ten."
quests.explanation: Nine is under ten, so a nine-year-old must wear the armband.
quests.evidenceLine: At the swimming pool, children under ten must wear a bright orange armband.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The old bridge in our town was built in 1890. It was closed for repairs in 2019 and opened again last spring.
quests.question: The old bridge is open again after repairs.
quests.hint: Read what happened after the repairs.
quests.explanation: The bridge opened again last spring, so it can be used after being repaired.
quests.evidenceLine: It was closed for repairs in 2019 and opened again last spring.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The number 12 bus runs every ten minutes on weekdays. On weekends, it comes only every twenty minutes.
quests.question: The number 12 bus comes more often on weekends than on weekdays.
quests.hint: Compare weekdays with weekends.
quests.explanation: Every twenty minutes on weekends is less often than every ten minutes on weekdays.
quests.evidenceLine: The number 12 bus runs every ten minutes on weekdays. On weekends, it comes only every twenty minutes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Jana studies at night school two evenings a week. She has a two-hour class on Monday and another two-hour class on Wednesday.
quests.question: Jana spends four hours in class each week.
quests.hint: Add up the lengths of her classes.
quests.explanation: Two classes of two hours each make four hours.
quests.evidenceLine: She has a two-hour class on Monday and another two-hour class on Wednesday.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Mei's brother is three years older than she is. He is fifteen, and he goes to the same school as Mei.
quests.question: Mei is older than her brother.
quests.hint: Who is older, Mei or her brother?
quests.explanation: Her brother is three years older, so Mei is the younger one.
quests.evidenceLine: Mei's brother is three years older than she is.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Every night, Paolo puts his keys in a bowl by the door. He has not lost his keys once since he started doing this.
quests.question: Paolo's keys have stayed safe since he began using the bowl.
quests.hint: Read what has happened since the habit started.
quests.explanation: He has not lost his keys once since he began the habit, so they have stayed safe.
quests.evidenceLine: He has not lost his keys once since he started doing this.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Mina's tablet needs to charge for three hours. After that, the battery lasts for about ten hours.
quests.question: A full charge gives Mina's tablet about ten hours of use.
quests.hint: Look at how long the battery lasts.
quests.explanation: The battery lasts about ten hours after the three-hour charge.
quests.evidenceLine: After that, the battery lasts for about ten hours.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The ferry from Split to the island leaves at 8 a.m. and again at 4 p.m. The trip takes about ninety minutes.
quests.question: There is only one ferry each day.
quests.hint: Count the departure times.
quests.explanation: Two times are given, 8 a.m. and 4 p.m., so the ferry runs twice.
quests.evidenceLine: The ferry from Split to the island leaves at 8 a.m. and again at 4 p.m.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Sofia earns $12 an hour at her weekend job in a bookstore. Last Saturday she worked for five hours.
quests.question: Sofia earned $60 last Saturday.
quests.hint: Think about her hourly pay and her hours.
quests.explanation: Five hours at $12 an hour comes to $60.
quests.evidenceLine: Sofia earns $12 an hour at her weekend job in a bookstore. Last Saturday she worked for five hours.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The Garcias' new house has a small kitchen but a very large living room. They plan to paint the living room yellow next month.
quests.question: The Garcias' kitchen is bigger than their living room.
quests.hint: Compare the two rooms.
quests.explanation: The kitchen is small and the living room is very large, so it is the other way around.
quests.evidenceLine: The Garcias' new house has a small kitchen but a very large living room.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: In many countries, people bring a small gift when they visit someone's home. Flowers and sweets are common choices.
quests.question: Guests often bring flowers or sweets to a home.
quests.hint: Look at the gifts named in the passage.
quests.explanation: Flowers and sweets are named as common gifts for visitors.
quests.evidenceLine: Flowers and sweets are common choices.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Plastic bags take hundreds of years to break down. Many stores now charge five cents for each bag to encourage people to bring their own.
quests.question: Some stores make customers pay for plastic bags.
quests.hint: Look at what many stores now do.
quests.explanation: Many stores charge five cents a bag, so some stores do ask for payment.
quests.evidenceLine: Many stores now charge five cents for each bag to encourage people to bring their own.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Basil grows best in warm weather with plenty of sun. Ken keeps his basil plant on a sunny windowsill and waters it twice a week.
quests.question: Ken keeps his basil in a dark corner.
quests.hint: Where is the basil plant?
quests.explanation: The plant sits on a sunny windowsill, not in a dark corner.
quests.evidenceLine: Ken keeps his basil plant on a sunny windowsill and waters it twice a week.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The local radio station plays news every hour and music in between. Its most popular show is on Saturday mornings.
quests.question: The station plays the news once a day.
quests.hint: How often is the news played?
quests.explanation: The news comes every hour, which is far more often than once a day.
quests.evidenceLine: The local radio station plays news every hour and music in between.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Rana's computer became very slow last month. Her cousin deleted old files and restarted it, and now it works fast again.
quests.question: Rana solved the slowness without help from anyone else.
quests.hint: Read how the problem was solved.
quests.explanation: Her cousin deleted old files and restarted the computer, so she had help.
quests.evidenceLine: Her cousin deleted old files and restarted it, and now it works fast again.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Weather forecasters said it would be sunny all week. But on Wednesday afternoon, heavy rain surprised everyone in the park.
quests.question: The forecast was wrong on Wednesday.
quests.hint: Compare what was predicted with what happened.
quests.explanation: Sunny weather was predicted for the whole week, yet heavy rain fell on Wednesday.
quests.evidenceLine: Weather forecasters said it would be sunny all week. But on Wednesday afternoon, heavy rain surprised everyone in the park.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Diego speaks Spanish at home and English at work. He is now learning French because he wants to move to Paris next year.
quests.question: Diego plans to move to Paris this month.
quests.hint: Find when the move will happen.
quests.explanation: The move is planned for next year, not this month.
quests.evidenceLine: He is now learning French because he wants to move to Paris next year.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The art class at the community center meets on Thursday evenings. Students bring their own paper, but the center gives them paint and brushes.
quests.question: Students have to bring their own paint.
quests.hint: Who provides the paint?
quests.explanation: The center provides the paint and brushes. Students only bring paper.
quests.evidenceLine: Students bring their own paper, but the center gives them paint and brushes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Lucia pays $900 a month in rent for her apartment. Her monthly bills for electricity and internet together are $120.
quests.question: Rent and bills together cost Lucia less than $1,000 a month.
quests.hint: Add the rent and the bills.
quests.explanation: $900 plus $120 is $1,020, which is more than $1,000.
quests.evidenceLine: Lucia pays $900 a month in rent for her apartment. Her monthly bills for electricity and internet together are $120.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Karl's apartment has one bedroom. He sleeps there, but he works at a desk near the living room window.
quests.question: Karl works in the living room.
quests.hint: Where is Karl's desk?
quests.explanation: His desk is near the living room window, so he works in that room.
quests.evidenceLine: He sleeps there, but he works at a desk near the living room window.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Farah opened a bakery three years ago. At first she had two workers, but now she has eight.
quests.question: Farah's bakery has more workers now than at the start.
quests.hint: Compare "at first" with "now."
quests.explanation: Two workers grew to eight, so there are more today.
quests.evidenceLine: At first she had two workers, but now she has eight.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The city library is open until 8 p.m. on weekdays. On Saturdays it closes at 4 p.m., and on Sundays it is closed.
quests.question: The library closes earlier on weekdays than on Saturdays.
quests.hint: Compare the closing times.
quests.explanation: It closes at 8 p.m. on weekdays but at 4 p.m. on Saturdays, so Saturday is earlier.
quests.evidenceLine: The city library is open until 8 p.m. on weekdays. On Saturdays it closes at 4 p.m., and on Sundays it is closed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: During the harvest festival, villagers cook a large meal and share it with everyone. Music and dancing begin after dinner and continue until midnight.
quests.question: The dancing starts before the meal.
quests.hint: Which comes first, the dinner or the dancing?
quests.explanation: Dancing begins after dinner, not before it.
quests.evidenceLine: Music and dancing begin after dinner and continue until midnight.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The train to the coast takes two hours, but the bus takes three. Ali chose the bus because the ticket costs half as much.
quests.question: Ali's trip takes longer than it would by train.
quests.hint: Compare the two travel times.
quests.explanation: Ali took the bus, which takes three hours instead of two.
quests.evidenceLine: The train to the coast takes two hours, but the bus takes three. Ali chose the bus because the ticket costs half as much.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Solar panels on the school roof provide half of the school's electricity. The school plans to add more panels next year.
quests.question: The school gets some of its power from the sun.
quests.hint: Notice what the panels supply.
quests.explanation: Solar panels use sunlight, and they supply half of the school's electricity.
quests.evidenceLine: Solar panels on the school roof provide half of the school's electricity.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The first telephone was invented in the 1870s. Cell phones only became common in homes about a hundred years later.
quests.question: Cell phones became common in homes before the year 1900.
quests.hint: Add a hundred years to the 1870s.
quests.explanation: A hundred years after the 1870s is the 1970s, long after 1900.
quests.evidenceLine: Cell phones only became common in homes about a hundred years later.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The school soccer team won six games and lost two this season. The coach says the team played better than last year.
quests.question: The team lost more games than it won.
quests.hint: Compare the wins and the losses.
quests.explanation: Six wins is more than two losses.
quests.evidenceLine: The school soccer team won six games and lost two this season.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Nadia starts work at 8 a.m. and takes a one-hour lunch break at noon. She goes home at 5 p.m.
quests.question: Nadia is at work for nine hours each day.
quests.hint: Count from her start time to her finish time.
quests.explanation: From 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. is nine hours, including the lunch break.
quests.evidenceLine: Nadia starts work at 8 a.m. and takes a one-hour lunch break at noon. She goes home at 5 p.m.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Oscar's grandparents live in the country. The family visits them every summer and stays for two weeks.
quests.question: Oscar's family sees his grandparents in the summer.
quests.hint: When does the family go to the country?
quests.explanation: They visit every summer, so they see the grandparents then.
quests.evidenceLine: The family visits them every summer and stays for two weeks.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Before leaving the house, Jim checks that the stove is off. Then he locks the door and tests the handle twice.
quests.question: Jim locks the door before he checks the stove.
quests.hint: Think about Jim's first action.
quests.explanation: He checks the stove first, and locking the door comes afterward.
quests.evidenceLine: Before leaving the house, Jim checks that the stove is off. Then he locks the door and tests the handle twice.
